key_insight: A physics-informed variational quantum classifier can learn interpretable interferometric parameters to distinguish strongly correlated quantum phases, specifically the Fermi polaron and molecular bound-state transition.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a scalable, hardware-executable route to quantum phase detection with linear gate complexity, making it attractive for quantum sensing and many-body state characterization.
method: Builds a variational classifier from Trotterised time evolution of an effective Hamiltonian
Learns physically meaningful parameters such as evolution time and bath interactions
Uses Ramsey-fringe visibility to separate BEC and BCS regimes
evidence_signal: The classifier was validated on the QRed superconducting quantum processor and maintained the correct relative ordering of the topological phases despite noise and decoherence.
watch_item: Performance on real hardware remains sensitive to noise, decoherence, and the fidelity of the effective Hamiltonian model.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Variational Quantum Classifier for Phase Detection in Strongly Correlated Matter
